title: *Fear of Data* - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Cowen recommends Omri Ben-Shahar's book Fear of Data, which argues privacy panic has led tech regulation astray and that privacy should get less weight in social decisions, citing benefits like facial recognition in trafficking investigations.

insights.claim: Omri Ben-Shahar's book Fear of Data argues that privacy panic has led tech regulation astray and that privacy considerations should receive less weight in social decisions.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: An intellectual case for loosening privacy regulation could support data-intensive tech and AI business models.
insights.quote: Basically the author wishes to give privacy considerations less weight in social decisions.

insights.claim: The book highlights that facial recognition technology aids human-trafficking investigations, though global estimates of victims rescued are lacking.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Benefit side of surveillance tech is under-measured, weakening cost-benefit debates on bans.

insights.claim: A chapter titled 'The Futility of Personal Rights' challenges the individual-rights approach to data privacy.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Signals a growing intellectual counter-current to rights-based privacy regimes like consent frameworks.
insights.quote: One chapter is entitled “The Futility of Personal Rights.”
